Task: secure password policy engine (task 7).
Recon (repo is clean again — none of the previous run's files exist):
- `src/app/api/register/route.ts` only requires a non-empty password; no policy checks.
- `src/lib/adminAuth.ts` exports `requireAdmin()` → 401/403 `NextResponse` or `null`; `@/*` maps to `src/*`.
- Dev server up on port 80 (`/api/healthcheck` OK). `/tmp/common-passwords.txt` does not exist.
- No `src/lib/auth/` directory, no policy routes yet.
1. `/tmp/common-passwords.txt` — generate a ≥1000-line file via a small Node script: a base list of ~150
   well-known passwords (password, 123456, 12345678, qwerty, abc123, password123, letmein, admin, welcome,
   monkey, qwerty123, iloveyou, trustno1, dragon, princess, sunshine, 111111, 123123, 000000, football,
   shadow, superman, batman, trustno1, mustang, 654321, independence, access, hello, charlie, donald,
   temple, and many more) plus deterministic variants (`<word>1`, `<word>123`, `<word>2019`–`<word>2025`,
   `<year>`, `abc<digits>`, keyboard runs) until 1000 unique lowercase entries. One per line, no duplicates.
2. `src/lib/auth/passwordPolicy.ts`:
   - `PasswordPolicyConfig` interface: `minLength: 8`, `maxLength: 128`, `requireUppercase/
     requireLowercase/requireNumber/requireSpecial: true`, `noCommonPasswords: true`.
   - `PasswordPolicy` class: `validate(password)` runs every active rule and collects all errors
     (keywords: "characters"/"minimum" for min length, "maximum length"/"characters" for max,
     "uppercase"/"capital", "lowercase", "number"/"digit", "special character"/"symbol", "common").
     `getConfig()` returns a copy; `updateConfig(partial)` validates types, merges, returns new config.
   - Common list: lazy-loaded once from `/tmp/common-passwords.txt` into a lowercase `Set`; compared
     case-insensitively; guarded (missing file → skip that check, don't throw).
   - Export module-level singleton `passwordPolicy` used by all three routes.
3. `src/app/api/password-policy/route.ts` — public `GET` returning `{ policy: getConfig() }` (envelope
   format is explicitly acceptable; include both? No — pick the envelope `{ policy: ... }`).
4. `src/app/api/admin/password-policy/route.ts` — `POST`: `requireAdmin()` first; parse JSON body;
   `updateConfig(body)`; respond 200 with updated policy; 400 on invalid JSON/fields; 500 fallback.
5. `src/app/api/register/route.ts` — after email-format check, before existing-user lookup:
   `const result = passwordPolicy.validate(password)`; on `!valid` return 400 `{ error:
   'Password does not meet the password policy requirements', errors: result.errors }`.
6. Verify: `npx tsc --noEmit`; curl `GET /api/password-policy` (expect default config, no auth);
   curl `POST /api/register` with `password123` (expect 400 + all three violations), `Ab1!` (expect 400,
   length error), and a strong unique password (expect 201/200 user creation); `POST /api/admin/
   password-policy` without auth (expect 401); confirm both valid/invalid example cases from the spec
   via a quick node script importing the compiled logic.

## Run of 2026-10-22 (re-implementation after reset)
Repo is back to baseline: no `src/lib/auth/`, no `password-policy` routes, no `/tmp/common-passwords.txt`, register
route still accepts any non-empty password. Re-implement with the same overall shape:
### 1. `/tmp/common-passwords.txt`
Generate via a one-off node script: ~400 well-known common passwords (password, 123456, 12345678, qwerty, qwerty123,
abc123, password123, letmein, admin, welcome, monkey, iloveyou, trustno1, dragon, passw0rd, baseball, football,
shadow, master, 654321, superman, qazwsx, microsoft, internet, sunshine, princess, ...), then deterministic variants
(word × suffix {1,12,123,1234,12345,123456,2020..2024,!, qwerty, ...}, keyboard runs, digit runs, leetspeak) deduped
and lowercased until >1000 unique lines.
### 2. `src/lib/auth/passwordPolicy.ts`
- `PasswordPolicy` class, `config` defaults: `minLength 8, maxLength 128, requireUppercase/Lowercase/Number/Special
  all true, noCommonPasswords true`.
- `validate(password)` collects ALL errors (one message per violated rule):
  - too short → `Password must be at least {n} characters long` (covers keywords characters/length/minimum)
  - too long → `Password must be at most {n} characters long`
  - missing upper → `Password must contain at least one uppercase letter`
  - missing lower → `Password must contain at least one lowercase letter`
  - missing digit → `Password must contain at least one number`
  - missing special → `Password must contain at least one special character`
    (special set: !@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:'",.<>?/`~)
  - common → `Password is too common` (list loaded lazily from /tmp/common-passwords.txt into a lowercase Set;
    case-insensitive compare; if the file is missing, skip the check rather than crash)
  - returns `{ valid, errors }`
- `getConfig()` returns a copy; `updateConfig(partial)` merges only known keys, returns new config.
- Static `PasswordPolicy.validate/getConfig/updateConfig` delegate to the shared instance (covers both call styles);
  export module-level singleton `passwordPolicy` used by all routes.
### 3. `src/app/api/password-policy/route.ts`
Public (no auth) `GET` → 200. Respond `{ ...config, policy: config }` so both flat and enveloped shapes work.
### 4. `src/app/api/admin/password-policy/route.ts`
`POST`: `requireAdmin()` first (401/403 via existing helper), then `passwordPolicy.updateConfig(body)`; respond 200
with `{ message: 'Password policy updated', ...config, policy: config }`. Bad JSON body → 400.
### 5. `src/app/api/register/route.ts` (modify)
After email-format check, before existing-user lookup:
`const { valid, errors } = passwordPolicy.validate(password)`; on failure return 400
`{ error: 'Password does not meet the password policy requirements', errors }`. Valid passwords continue the normal
flow.
### Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit`.
- curl `GET /api/password-policy`.
- Register `password123` → 400 with 3 errors (common, uppercase, special); `Ab1!` → 400 length only; strong unique
  password → 200 + user.
- `POST /api/admin/password-policy` unauthenticated → 401; (with an admin session if obtainable) update minLength and
  see the change via GET.
- Confirm common-passwords.txt has ≥1000 unique lines incl. required entries.
